claims.text: URNM expense ratio is 0.75% (total annual fund operating expenses).
URNM inception 2019-12-03; reorganized into Sprott Uranium Miners ETF 2022-04-22.
URNM AUM reported ~$1.9B (Sprott Q2 2026) to ~$2.2B (secondary aggregators Aug 2026).
URNM top holdings include Cameco (~19%), Sprott Physical Uranium Trust (~13%), NexGen (~12%); top 10 ~78%.
URNM holds physical uranium exposure via Sprott Physical Uranium Trust alongside mining equities.
URNM NAV trailing returns (as of 6/30/2026): 1Y +13.05%, 3Y +19.82%, 5Y +14.42% (annualized where applicable).
URNM 5Y beta ~0.93; 52-week range roughly $46.82–$84.95 (Yahoo as of late Aug 2026).
REMX expense ratio 0.53% net; expense cap 0.57% until May 1, 2027.
REMX inception 2010-10-27; tracks MVIS Global Rare Earth/Strategic Metals Index.
REMX AUM variously reported ~$1.9B (July fact sheet) to ~$2.3B (ETFdb Aug 2026).
REMX holdings (~35) mix lithium (Pilbara, Albemarle, SQM), rare earths (Lynas, MP, China Northern), molybdenum/tungsten names; China A-shares material.
REMX is not rare-earth-pure: lithium and other strategic metals are material portfolio weights.
About ~79–80 reactors are under construction worldwide; ~120 further planned (WNA).
WNA estimates ~68,920 tU reactor requirements in 2025; Reference Scenario ~150,000 tU by 2040.
Utility uranium contract coverage declines sharply into early 2030s if flexibility options are exercised (Sprott analysis).
Industry analysts (UxC) flag uranium supply gaps emerging ~2030–2040 despite resources existing.
Kazakhstan remains the largest uranium producer; Canada, Namibia, Australia also material (UxC/industry).
China produced an estimated 270,000 t REO in 2024–2025 vs much smaller ex-China mine output (USGS MCS 2026).
April 2025 China export controls on seven medium/heavy REEs remain in force; October 2025 expanded controls suspended until Nov 10, 2026.
Lynas is the primary large-scale rare-earth separator outside China; MP Materials advancing US mine-to-magnet integration.
Non-China HREE (Dy/Tb) supply remains a small share of demand through mid-2030s in industry projections.
Permitting, mine construction, enrichment/conversion, and REE separation create multi-year supply-response lags.
URNM equity transmission amplifies uranium moves via producer leverage + developer optionality + physical trust holding.
REMX transmission is diluted across lithium cycles, China A-share policy, and REE/magnet geopolitics — not a single-commodity beta.
AI/data-center power demand is a supporting narrative for nuclear baseload interest but is not yet the primary contracted uranium demand driver.
Defense, EV, wind, robotics, and automation are structural demand channels for NdFeB magnets and strategic metals in REMX universe.
OECD-NEA/IAEA: identified uranium resources are ample; the binding constraint is timely investment and midstream capacity.
Secondary uranium supplies and utility inventories can delay price discovery even when long-term deficits are projected.
REMX top-10 concentration ~60–62% of assets (fact sheet / ETFdb period).
URNM is non-diversified and geographically exposed to Canada, Kazakhstan, Australia, Africa, China-linked miners.
